categories.name: FoodTech
categories.description: Food technology, safety, and supply chain innovation

questions.text: What food safety certifications have you achieved?
questions.helpText: Track GFSI-recognized food safety standards. IRL 1-2: Developing HACCP, IRL 3-4: HACCP certified, IRL 5-6: SQF/BRC Level 1-2, IRL 7-8: SQF/BRC Level 3 or FSSC 22000, IRL 9: Multiple sites with AA+ ratings

options.text: Developing HACCP plan or food safety program
HACCP certified or equivalent basic food safety certification
SQF/BRC/IFS Level 1-2 or similar GFSI-recognized standard
SQF Level 3, BRC A-grade, or FSSC 22000 certified
BRC AA-grade or SQF Excellence rating at single facility
Multiple facilities with top-tier certifications (AA+ ratings) and zero recalls

questions.text: What is your supply chain traceability capability?
questions.helpText: Measure end-to-end traceability and recall readiness. IRL 1-2: Manual records, IRL 3-4: Digital batch tracking, IRL 5-6: Real-time tracking (<4 hours recall), IRL 7-8: Blockchain/IoT tracking (<1 hour recall), IRL 9: Full farm-to-fork transparency

options.text: Manual paper-based record keeping
Digital batch tracking with basic traceability (24-48 hours)
ERP-integrated tracking with <24 hour recall capability
Real-time tracking with <4 hour recall capability
IoT/blockchain tracking with <1 hour recall and supplier verification
Full farm-to-fork transparency with consumer-facing traceability

questions.text: What shelf life extension or preservation technology have you achieved?
questions.helpText: Measure proven shelf life extension %. IRL 1-2: Lab testing, IRL 3-4: 10-25% extension validated, IRL 5-6: 25-50% extension in market, IRL 7-8: 50-100% extension with major customers, IRL 9: Industry-leading preservation (100%+ extension)

options.text: Lab-based shelf life testing
10-25% shelf life extension validated in controlled studies
25-50% extension with pilot customers (accelerated testing)
50-75% extension with commercial customers (real-time validation)
75-100% extension with major food manufacturers or retailers
100%+ extension (doubling shelf life) with published efficacy data

questions.text: What measurable food waste reduction have you delivered?
questions.helpText: Track tons of food waste prevented annually. IRL 1-2: Planning/estimating, IRL 3-4: <100 tons/year, IRL 5-6: 100-1K tons/year, IRL 7-8: 1K-10K tons/year, IRL 9: 10K+ tons/year with third-party verification

options.text: Planning waste reduction methodology
<100 tons food waste prevented annually (measured)
100-1,000 tons prevented annually with customer validation
1,000-10,000 tons prevented with third-party audit
10,000-50,000 tons prevented with published impact reports
50,000+ tons prevented annually with verified environmental impact

questions.text: What food regulatory approvals have you obtained?
questions.helpText: Track FDA, USDA, EU, or equivalent approvals. IRL 1-2: Pre-market testing, IRL 3-4: GRAS notification or equivalent, IRL 5-6: FDA/USDA approval (single region), IRL 7-8: Multi-region approvals, IRL 9: Global approvals (US, EU, Asia)

options.text: Pre-market testing and regulatory strategy development
GRAS self-affirmation or equivalent safety determination
FDA GRAS notice filed or EU novel food consultation submitted
FDA/USDA approval or EU novel food authorization in one region
Approvals in multiple major markets (US + EU, or US + Asia)
Global regulatory approvals (US, EU, China, Japan) with ongoing compliance

questions.text: What is your alternative protein production scale? (if applicable)
questions.helpText: For alt-protein companies, measure production capacity (tons/year). IRL 1-2: Lab scale (<1 ton), IRL 3-4: Pilot scale (1-100 tons), IRL 5-6: Commercial scale (100-1K tons), IRL 7-8: Industrial scale (1K-10K tons), IRL 9: Mass market scale (10K+ tons)

options.text: Lab-scale production (<1 ton/year)
Pilot-scale production (1-10 tons/year)
Pre-commercial scale (10-100 tons/year)
Commercial scale (100-1,000 tons/year) with co-packer
Industrial scale (1,000-10,000 tons/year) with own facility
Mass market scale (10,000+ tons/year) with multiple facilities

questions.text: What is your retail and foodservice distribution?
questions.helpText: Track retail doors and foodservice locations. IRL 1-2: Direct-to-consumer, IRL 3-4: <100 doors/locations, IRL 5-6: 100-1K doors, IRL 7-8: 1K-10K doors (regional chains), IRL 9: 10K+ doors (national/international)

options.text: Direct-to-consumer or farmers markets only
<100 retail doors or foodservice locations (local)
100-1,000 doors (regional specialty retailers or restaurants)
1,000-5,000 doors (regional chain or national specialty)
5,000-10,000 doors (national chain or multiple channels)
10,000+ doors (multiple national chains, international expansion)

questions.text: What consumer acceptance testing have you conducted?
questions.helpText: Measure consumer testing rigor and results. IRL 1-2: Internal tasting, IRL 3-4: <100 consumers, IRL 5-6: 100-500 consumers with purchase intent, IRL 7-8: 500+ with repeat purchase data, IRL 9: Multi-market testing with high Net Promoter Score

options.text: Internal team or friends & family tasting
<100 consumer tastings with basic feedback
100-500 consumers with quantitative surveys (acceptance, purchase intent)
500-1,000 consumers with validated purchase intent (>60%)
1,000+ consumers with repeat purchase data and NPS >30
Multi-market testing (5,000+ consumers) with NPS >50 and brand tracking

questions.text: What sustainability metrics can you demonstrate vs. conventional products?
questions.helpText: Track LCA-validated environmental improvements. IRL 1-2: Estimating impact, IRL 3-4: Internal LCA, IRL 5-6: Third-party LCA (ISO 14040), IRL 7-8: Multiple categories (water, land, GHG), IRL 9: Published peer-reviewed sustainability data

options.text: Estimating sustainability benefits vs. conventional
Internal life cycle assessment (LCA) completed
Third-party verified LCA showing improvement in one category
ISO 14040-compliant LCA showing improvements in 2-3 categories (GHG, water, land)
Comprehensive LCA with EPD and 30-50% reductions across multiple metrics
Peer-reviewed published LCA showing 50-90% reductions, industry benchmark

questions.text: What is your production cost vs. conventional products?
questions.helpText: Compare COGS to conventional equivalents. IRL 1-2: High cost (3-10x), IRL 3-4: Premium (2-3x), IRL 5-6: Moderate premium (1.5-2x), IRL 7-8: Near parity (1-1.5x), IRL 9: Cost competitive or below (<1x)

options.text: Very high cost (3-10x conventional) at lab scale
High premium (2-3x conventional) at pilot scale
Moderate premium (1.5-2x) at initial commercial scale
Approaching parity (1-1.5x) with scale and optimization
Near parity or slight premium (0.9-1.1x) at industrial scale
Cost competitive or below conventional (<0.9x) at mass market scale

questions.text: What is your ingredient sourcing and supplier qualification status?
questions.helpText: Track supplier quality programs and dual sourcing. IRL 1-2: Single unaudited suppliers, IRL 3-4: Audited suppliers, IRL 5-6: Dual sourcing for critical ingredients, IRL 7-8: Supplier quality program with scorecards, IRL 9: Vertical integration or strategic partnerships

options.text: Single-source suppliers, no formal qualification
Supplier audits conducted, basic qualification program
Dual sourcing for some critical ingredients, documented qualification
Dual sourcing for all critical ingredients, annual audits, contingency plans
Supplier quality program with scorecards, performance monitoring, continuous improvement
Vertical integration or strategic partnerships with key suppliers, supply chain resilience

questions.text: What quality control and testing systems do you have?
questions.helpText: Assess QC testing frequency and scope. IRL 1-2: Manual spot checks, IRL 3-4: Batch testing, IRL 5-6: In-line monitoring, IRL 7-8: Automated QC with SPC, IRL 9: Real-time quality analytics with predictive maintenance

options.text: Manual spot checks or visual inspection
Batch testing with documented QC procedures
In-line monitoring with hold-and-release protocols
Automated QC systems with statistical process control (SPC)
Real-time monitoring with automated alerts and corrective actions
AI-powered quality analytics with predictive issue detection and zero defects

questions.text: What is your cold chain management and temperature monitoring?
questions.helpText: For temperature-sensitive products, track cold chain integrity. IRL 1-2: Basic cold storage, IRL 3-4: Manual temperature logs, IRL 5-6: Automated monitoring, IRL 7-8: IoT sensors with alerts, IRL 9: End-to-end cold chain visibility

options.text: Basic cold storage with periodic checks
Manual temperature logging at key points
Automated temperature monitoring in facilities
IoT sensors in transport with real-time alerts and deviation tracking
End-to-end cold chain monitoring from production to retail with automated alerts
Full supply chain visibility with predictive analytics and <0.1% cold chain failures

questions.text: What is your brand recognition and consumer awareness?
questions.helpText: Measure aided/unaided brand awareness. IRL 1-2: No brand tracking, IRL 3-4: Local awareness (<5%), IRL 5-6: Regional awareness (5-15%), IRL 7-8: National awareness (15-30%), IRL 9: Category leader (30%+ awareness)

options.text: No brand awareness tracking
Local brand awareness (<5% aided awareness)
Regional brand awareness (5-15% aided awareness)
National brand tracking with 15-30% aided awareness
Strong national brand with 30-50% aided awareness and 10%+ unaided
Category-leading brand with 50%+ aided awareness and 20%+ unaided

questions.text: What proprietary food technology or IP do you have?
questions.helpText: Track patents, trade secrets, and process innovation. IRL 1-2: No IP, IRL 3-4: Patents pending, IRL 5-6: Granted patents (1-5), IRL 7-8: Patent portfolio (5-15), IRL 9: Strong IP moat (15+ patents, trade secrets)

options.text: No proprietary technology or IP filings
1-2 provisional or utility patents pending
1-5 patents granted or pending with trade secret protection
5-10 patents with international protection and validated FTO
10-20 patents with strong portfolio and proprietary processes
20+ patents with blocking IP, trade secrets, and potential licensing revenue
